summary: A 15 s, time-coded plan for a 9:16 TikTok/Reels promo of Oakley OX8208 (kit kits/2026-09-21_ox8208-0552, Matt Abyss, paired with Essilor Eyezen + Crizal Prevencia). It wants to sell the frame through a soft intro, a product shot, a benefit line and a price card. The 15 s length, the 9:16 format and the real in-stock SKU fit the brief. But the plan has five critical failures: two health/product claims with no support ('Blocks 100% blue light', 'protects kids from myopia'), a made-up price/promo when the brief says no price was given, Thai on-screen text in an English-only product clip, and no Oakley partner logo. It also breaks most clip house rules: store line art, a busy background, a single angle when two plus a lens layer exist, a slow fade opening, a song baked into the export, and key text below the safe zone. Verdict: fail. A rebuild from the beat-clip reference is needed, not a patch.

findings.problem: Product claim is false for this lens pairing. The kit's coating, Crizal Prevencia, filters about 20% of 400-455 nm blue-violet per the maker. Nothing in data/ says 100%.
findings.why: Unsupported product claim: product claims need maker data, labelled, and checked against independent evidence; '100%' wording is banned. claims_library C01: blue-cut benefits are unsupported (Cochrane 2023, AAO).
findings.ref: creative-intelligence/knowledge/optical/FACT_CHECK_WORKFLOW.md (row D product claim + wording table); claims_library.json C01; kits/2026-09-21_ox8208-0552/kit.md (lens + coating)
findings.fix: Drop the line, or use maker wording only, labelled: "Crizal Prevencia: filters part of blue-violet light + UV protection (maker data)". No percentages beyond the maker's 20% and no benefit claims.

findings.problem: Health claim with no support. The paired lenses are not myopia-control lenses, and the HSTN SQ RX is an adult frame. Even real myopia-control lenses only slow progression; they do not 'protect' children.
findings.why: False/unsupported health claim. claims_library C19: only DIMS/HAL lenses have evidence, and they slow myopia without stopping it. C02: blue light is not shown to harm eyes.
findings.fix: Remove it. This clip has no basis for any myopia or kids claim.

findings.location: 12.0-15.0 s, line 6: price card "฿1,990 only this week!"
findings.problem: Price and time-limited promo are made up. The brief says the user has not given a price.
findings.why: Never invent a price/promo; ask for the price each promo clip
findings.ref: tas-20260925-003; CLAUDE.md house rules; .claude/skills/beat-clip/SKILL.md House rules ('Price/promo only when the user gives it')
findings.fix: Ask the user for the price/promo before building. Until then, end on the TIMEOPTIC wordmark with no price card.

findings.location: 5.0-9.0 s, line 4: text "แว่นสวย ราคาดี"
findings.problem: Thai on-screen text in a product clip. 'ราคาดี' (good price) also implies a price claim.
findings.why: Product clips are English-only (house rule: language)
findings.ref: tas-20260925-002; beat-clip SKILL.md 'English only on screen and in captions'
findings.fix: Use English only, with text taken from data/: e.g. "OAKLEY HSTN SQ RX" / "Matt Abyss" / lens name.

findings.problem: The partner logo is missing for the whole clip, even though brand/partner-logos/oakley.svg exists (also kits/2026-09-21_ox8208-0552/photos/oakley.svg).
findings.why: Clips carry the frame brand's logo top-left (left 64 px, top 64 px) for the whole clip (house rule: logo)
findings.ref: tas-20260925-001; beat-clip SKILL.md 'Brand logo of the frame right in the top-left corner'
findings.fix: Place brand/partner-logos/oakley.svg at left 64 / top 64 for 0-15 s, with an explicit width and height on the .

findings.location: 2.0-5.0 s, line 3: "floating line-art doodles of the store"
findings.problem: Store line art in a clip.
findings.why: No storefront line art in clips (user, 2026-09-25)
findings.ref: tas-20260925-001; beat-clip SKILL.md TIMEOPTIC wordmark rule ('No storefront line art in clips')
findings.fix: Remove the doodles. The brand is carried by the moving wordmark instead.

findings.problem: A busy background competes with a matt navy and translucent blue frame. The kit notes that the translucent lower rim blends into dark grounds.
findings.why: Calm backgrounds so the glasses stand out. kit.md layer note: light or mid grounds work best; add a rim light on dark ones.
findings.fix: Use a calm light or mid-tone ground (or a soft cool gradient), with a rim light if dark.

findings.location: 9.0-12.0 s, line 5: "one static front shot (only angle available)"
findings.problem: Factually wrong and against the rule. The kit has two angles (front OX8208-0552_1 and three-quarter OX8208-0552_2 with the temple logo). There are no detail punch-ins and the shot is static.
findings.why: Several angles plus one detail punch-in per beat; missing angles should be sourced from the web
findings.fix: Cut on the beat between front, three-quarter and punch-ins (temple metal logo, keyhole bridge, two-tone brow/rim). Look for side and other angles of the same model and colour on the web.

findings.location: 9.0-12.0 s, line 5: "cutout glasses with empty lens area (no lens layer)"
findings.problem: Empty lenses make the cutout look hollow. A lens layer already exists: layers/OX8208-0552_1_lens.png.
findings.ref: CLAUDE.md house rules; beat-clip SKILL.md 'Lens layer on every cutout'
findings.fix: Add OX8208-0552_1_lens.png. Build a lens mask for _2 (alpha holes > 40, components > 5000 px, dilate 5 px).

findings.problem: The opening is a slow fade with nothing on screen for the first beats, which loses viewers in the first second.
findings.why: Hook rule: frame 0 is the most striking shot, slammed in with an impact; never a slow fade
findings.fix: Open on a detail close-up (the Oakley metal temple logo from _2) with over-scale, blur and flash snapping in ~0.15 s plus impact-bass at t=0.

findings.problem: The brand appears as a static one-word "TimeOptic" at the start. The rule asks for the spaced, moving TIMEOPTIC wordmark (letters in, shine) ending big in the centre.
findings.why: Moving spaced TIMEOPTIC wordmark; 'Time Optic' two words in running text
findings.ref: tas-20260925-001; beat-clip SKILL.md TIMEOPTIC wordmark rule (LOGO_GAP)
findings.fix: Move the brand moment to the end (about 12-15 s) using the letter-slice wordmark with a 12 px TIME-OPTIC gap and a shine sweep.

findings.location: 12.0-15.0 s, line 6: price card at y = 1700 px
findings.problem: Key text sits under the TikTok/Reels caption UI and will be covered.
findings.why: Safe zone x 60-940, y 220-1480; key text in y 300-1400
findings.ref: beat-clip SKILL.md 'TikTok UI safe zone'; STUDIO_RULES
findings.fix: Keep all type and logos (bar the top-left partner logo) inside y 220-1480 and key text in y 300-1400. Check with the drawbox contact sheet.

findings.location: line 7: "final song mixed into the export"; line 2: "soft piano intro"
findings.problem: The song is baked into the upload file. The rule says the user adds music in the app; a ripped song in the upload also risks copyright or mute.
findings.why: Music added by the user; beat clips deliver SFX-only plus a local preview with the song
findings.ref: tas-20260925-004; beat-clip SKILL.md step 6 (beat-audio.py: clip-hf.mp4 SFX-only + clip-hf_preview-song.mp4)
findings.fix: Pick a song from music/songs.md for the beat grid only. Deliver clip-hf.mp4 (SFX only) and clip-hf_preview-song.mp4 kept locally.

findings.problem: There is no BPM/beat grid, no SFX cues, and no product text from data/ (model HSTN SQ RX, colour Matt Abyss, lens Eyezen + Crizal Prevencia). Timings are round seconds, not beats.
findings.why: (craft) beat clips are built on B = 60/BPM with sections on beats; text only from data/
findings.ref: beat-clip SKILL.md steps 4-6 and 'Text only from data/'
findings.fix: Choose a song and BPM, re-time sections to beats, write clip-audio.json cues, and source all copy from kit.md.

strengths: The length (15 s) and the 9:16 TikTok/Reels format match the brief.
It uses a real in-stock SKU (OX8208-0552 is in data/frames/frames-stock-2026-09-15.csv) with an existing kit.
The plan is fully time-coded with no gaps, which makes it easy to fix section by section.
Using the cutout (real product photo) rather than an AI redraw keeps the product accurate.
opinion: A soft piano mood fits the sporty and street style tags of the HSTN SQ poorly; an upbeat, punchy track would probably suit it better. Test two songs with the user.
The cool navy and translucent blue colourway could drive a calm, cool-toned palette for the whole clip.

_withheld.why: Withheld: critical failures present (MASTER_QUALITY_SCORE.md §1 'any one = fix before delivery, no score'). Any later score is ai-judgement, not a human rating.
